text:
Alex: heads-up — nightly perf runner flagged repeated OOM-ish spikes on the long-context profiling job (gpt-like, seq=4096). attaching a tiny summary.
Meena: can you paste the kernel chooser trace? suspect mismatch between estimator and actual workspace use.
Alex: snippet from the runner log:
```
kernel_chooser: evaluated candidates [flashattn_v2, triton_attn, cublaslt_ffn]
estimates: flashattn_v2 -> 1.8GB, triton_attn -> 2.4GB, cublaslt_ffn -> 5.1GB
chosen: cublaslt_ffn (fallback) due to perf score for FFN at this batch shape
runtime_peak: 5.9GB (oom margin util 0.85)
```
Jin: whoa chosen=cublaslt_ffn for that shape? our heuristic should favor flashattn for attn + cublaslt only for ffn heavy models. maybe scoring weights skewed by inferred flops.
Sam: noticed this too after the canary rollout yesterday (rev a1b2fc). perf-regress alert triggered for p99 latency and memory pressure. canary logs show allocator reservations increasing mid-run.
Meena: attaching quick mem-account dump from the slab allocator. looks like kv cache & reserve counted twice during reserve probe window.
```
slab.total: 12.2GB
slab.active: 8.1GB
kv.pool_reserved: 1.6GB
kv.transient_reserve: 1.6GB  # same slab referenced twice
allocator.headroom_reserved: 0.9GB
```
Alex: if the KV pool increments a transient reserve while the slab already holds the backing buffer we double-count when computing free workspace -> chooser underestimates available headroom -> picks bigger kernel to be safe -> leads to cascade.
Jin: propose short-term mitigation: cap transient reserve to not exceed free_frag_region and reduce reserve when fragmentation > 25%.
Sam: I can spike a microbench. run this locally:
```
SIZER_DEBUG=1 python tools/bench/workspace_sweep.py --model=gpt-j --seq=4096 --batch=1 --rounds=20
```
Meena: and add gauges: `workspace_est_bytes`, `chosen_kernel`, `kv_pool_frag_pct`, `slab_free_bytes` to trace; that will help correlate estimator vs actual.
Alex: quick patch I sketched for the allocator (pseudo):
```
if kv_pool.fragmentation() > 0.25:
    kv_pool.transient_reserve = max(base_reserve * 0.5, min_reserve)
```
Jin: also suggest: when chooser receives >1 candidate with est within 10% of each other prefer lower-workspace kernel. prefer_flash = (est_flash <= 1.1 * est_other)
Sam: i'll run the bench with SIZER_DEBUG and post results here. if reproducible i'll open a rollback or restrict canary to 10% until we patch.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed: rollout rev=a1b2fc -> 15% hosts (2026-03-10T03:12:48Z) :rocket:
Meena: for long-term, we should also change accounting semantics: decouple backing buffer ownership from logical reserve so we don't double-count slab bytes in both `active` and `reserve` buckets.
Alex: agree. Sam, Jin — can you two pair on a small PR: (1) telemetry gauges, (2) cap transient reserve heuristic, (3) chooser tie-breaker favoring lower-workspace kernel. target: hotfix branch and small canary by EOD.
Sam: ack. opening issue & PR draft now, will tag @Jin and @Meena. adding perf test case in bench harness.
Jin: will add unit for fragmentation calc and a tiny simulation that asserts chosen_kernel changes when cap applied.
Meena: once PR lands, let's run a 4h longcontext soak on dedicated bench cluster. want to see p95/p99 and mem watermark.
Alex: thx all. added follow-up: file PERF-587 with logs and attach the nightly flame graph. I'll paste results after Sam's run. :thumbsup:
